layout_warnings: Pages 28-32 (the definitions/glossary appendix) print a header of 'Common Data Set 2019-2020', while pages 18-27 (the live survey) print 'Common Data Set 2021-2022'. Same physical document, same filing -- the glossary appendix simply carries a stale template-year header. Any heuristic that samples header text from a glossary page to determine the document's stated year will get the wrong year.

Page 20: the H1 dollar-amount table's cell values are extracted in a block disconnected from their row labels -- all dollar figures print together, category descriptions (Federal / State / Institutional / External) print in a separate later block. Naive top-to-bottom reading will misattribute amounts to the wrong row.

Page 25: the I-1 inclusion/exclusion definitional grid and the I-1 actual headcount table both use row letters A-J and sit back-to-back with no strong text-layer separator -- risk of merging the two distinct tables when keying by row letter alone.

Page 26: I-3 class-size table prints one shared bucket-header row (2-9...100+, Total) followed by two separate numeric blocks (Class Sections, then Class Subsections) with no repeated header between them -- risk of concatenating or cross-assigning the two blocks.

Page 27 (J1): row groups alternate between 2-line (Category, CIP code) and 3-line (Category, Bachelor's %, CIP code) depending on whether the discipline has a nonzero percentage -- there is no blank placeholder for a zero/absent percentage, so fixed-stride row parsing will drift after the first zero row.

Page 23 (H14): two side-by-side checklist columns ('Need Based Scholarships and Grants' vs. a non-need/loan list) are flattened into a single linear text run with the column headers detached from their item lists.

Section-heading codes that are page-anchors elsewhere (H1, H2, H4) also appear inside prose/instructions on other pages -- see section_anchor_notes below; a page-routing heuristic keyed on 'first occurrence of code X' will misroute to the prose page instead of the true heading page in several cases (e.g. 'H1' appears in prose on pages 20, 21, and 22, all before/after its true heading page 19).

text_layer_corruption.summary: Text layer for pages 18-32 is clean and machine-readable; no OCR garbling, no digit substitution/mangling observed in any dollar amount, percentage, or count. The only 'corruption'-adjacent issue is semantic, not character-level: the glossary appendix (pages 28-32) carries a leftover 'Common Data Set 2019-2020' header from an older template, inconsistent with the '2021-2022' header used on the live survey pages (18-27) of this same filing.
